items.title: Theory of Collaboration
items.description: We can reframe human collaboration as multiple agents working together to produce a common change in their environment, bound by a set of constraints. This allows us to view computer supported cooperative work (CSCW) systems as systems of computer-mediated interventions in processes of information exchange with the goal of adjusting or eliminating these constraints. This work explores how we can use this view to improve the human-computer interaction and design of computer-mediated collaborative systems.
items.question: How can we describe human collaboration in a way useful for designing computer-mediated interventions?

items.title: Survey of Collaborative Visualization
items.description: We are performing a comprehensive, systematic review of the publications in Collaborative Visualization to assess the current state of the research. We are exploring trends in the data visualization techniques used, and what collaborative setups have been studied. We are also looking at how inclusive sample research populations have been, as well as how rigorously researchers are reporting the metrics necessary for their science to be reproduceable.
items.question: What is the current state of research in Collaborative Data Visualization?

items.title: Reducing AI Bias in Collaboration
items.description: Explainable AI (XAI) is a powerful tool to highlight bias in the output from AI models, but most existing research focuses on a single human analyst. Insights gained from interpreting such highlights may not be carried over to collaborating analysts, especially in asynchronous hand-offs. This work explores the viability of using "interaction traces" to reduce bias propagation across collaborating analysts.
items.question: How can we reduce the propagation of AI bias across asynchronous handoffs between human collaborators?
